I'll write a single script that inspects all files, applies the targeted release changes, and cleans itself up.

{"action": "write", "path": "_release.py", "content": "import os, re, pathlib, sys

root = pathlib.Path('.')
files = ['pyproject.toml', 'src/fmt/__init__.py', 'README.md', 'CHANGELOG.md']
texts = {}
for f in files:
    texts[f] = (root / f).read_text()

print('=== ORIGINAL FILES ===')
for f in files:
    print('---', f, '---')
    print(texts[f])

new = '1.5.0'

# Determine current project version from pyproject.toml
m = re.search(r'^version\s*=\s*["\']([^"\']+)["\']', texts['pyproject.toml'], re.M)
if not m:
    print('ERROR: could not find version in pyproject.toml')
    sys.exit(1)
old = m.group(1)
print('OLD VERSION:', old)

# pyproject.toml: replace only the single version line
p = texts['pyproject.toml']
p2, n1 = re.subn(
    r'^version\s*=\s*["\']' + re.escape(old) + r'["\']',
    'version = "%s"' % new,
    p, count=1, flags=re.M)
print('pyproject replacements:', n1)
texts['pyproject.toml'] = p2

# src/fmt/__init__.py: replace __version__ assignment (allow optional type annotation)
i = texts['src/fmt/__init__.py']
i2, n2 = re.subn(
    r'(__version__\s*(?::\s*str\s*)?=\s*["\'])' + re.escape(old) + r'(["\'])',
    lambda mm: mm.group(1) + new + mm.group(2),
    i)
print('__init__ replacements:', n2)
texts['src/fmt/__init__.py'] = i2

# README.md: replace standalone occurrences of the project version (not embedded in longer versions)
r = texts['README.md']
r2, n3 = re.subn(r'(?<![\d.])' + re.escape(old) + r'(?![\d.])', new, r)
print('README replacements:', n3)
texts['README.md'] = r2

# CHANGELOG.md: insert new top entry after the header
entry = '## %s - 2026-11-04\n\n- Add the --json flag.\n\n' % new
c = texts['CHANGELOG.md']
if c.startswith('# Changelog\n\n'):
    c = '# Changelog\n\n' + entry + c[len('# Changelog\n\n'):]
else:
    print('ERROR: unexpected CHANGELOG header')
    sys.exit(1)
texts['CHANGELOG.md'] = c

# Write files back
for f in files:
    (root / f).write_text(texts[f])

print('=== MODIFIED FILES ===')
for f in files:
    print('---', f, '---')
    print(texts[f])

os.remove(__file__)
print('DONE')
"}

{"action": "run", "args": ["_release.py"]}
